note: Interim reading 2026-10-04 (day 9 of 14; the dated V5 record stays for 2026-10-09). Every per-session value below is a snapshot: the transcripts are live, so a later run reads different steps. `next_census.py --since 7 --repo /opt/fabrik` printed a bare `V5: PASS` before 95155b6f5; re-run after it, it prints `V5: PASS — 0 open next item(s) <= 0 qualifying session(s), 3 live claim(s)` — a vacuous pass. Classes line at the first run: 12797 NEXT lines over 1648 transcript files (names-item 1269, none 220, operator-decision 715, blocked 8, free-text 10585). Probe of 2026-10-03T23:13Z (scratch v5/final.py, census rules): 1656 files, 34 ending on a NEXT line (17 names-item, 7 none, 5 free-text, 5 operator-decision), 1622 carrying none. Its five session-final free-text values, none matching _is_anchor: a fabrik-lib session's in-progress review step ('when the T05 coder returns, pin its commit and start T05's full /fabrik-review.'), 'awaiting your reply — once the key is in .env, I run …' (trade-intelligence, main and a worktree), 'awaiting your reply' (youtube), and one hub value. Across five probe runs that afternoon every free-text final was a transient step or a wait, never a thread worth persisting. So on this small sample (n=5 per run) _is_anchor drops nothing worth keeping, and about half of the sessions that end on a NEXT name an item id. Caveat for the dated reading: the census counts NEXT lines more strictly than the harvest, counts every transcript file as a session and never counts the hub's worktree sessions — W-a9de5fb3 fixes that first. Second interim reading 2026-10-04T13:32Z (snapshot): next_census.py --since 7 --repo /opt/fabrik printed V5: PASS — 0 open next item(s) <= 3 qualifying session(s), 146 live claim(s). The right side is no longer 0 but the left side is, structurally: the store holds no open kind:next item in any tree (all 3 are dropped), so 0 <= N cannot fail and the PASS rests on live claims alone; and 144 of the 146 live claims were one infra session's batch claim at 13:31:36Z (2h lease), not adoption evidence. V5 compares two aggregate counts and never joins items to sessions. This run is on the census after W-a9de5fb3 (0fa538105: the harvest's NEXT rule, a session = a transcript with a main-thread assistant reply, hub worktree sessions keyed) and W-fae95bee (22747460a: shared-row ordering), so its counts are not comparable with the first reading's: 13606 NEXT lines over 1686 sessions (names-item 1593, none 224, operator-decision 753, blocked 8, free-text 11028); 17 sessions had at least one turn end on an accepted free-text NEXT. The dated record stays for 2026-10-09, and it is only informative if an open next item exists by then.
